2649	+import type { CategoryEntity } from '#types/models';
2650	+
2651	+export type CategoryWithSubcategories<T extends CategoryEntity> = T & {
2652	+  subcategories: T[];
2653	+};
2654	+
2655	+/**
2656	+ * Turns a group's flat category list into top-level categories, each with
2657	+ * its subcategories. Order is kept within each level. A subcategory is
2658	+ * shown as a top-level category when its parent isn't in the list
2659	+ * (deleted or in another group) or is itself a subcategory, which the
2660	+ * server doesn't allow but conflicting edits from two devices could
2661	+ * produce. That way a category never disappears.
2662	+ */
2663	+export function nestCategories<T extends CategoryEntity>(
2664	+  categories: T[],
2665	+): CategoryWithSubcategories<T>[] {
2666	+  const ids = new Set(categories.map(cat => cat.id));
2667	+  const hasValidParent = (cat: T) =>
2668	+    cat.parent_id != null && ids.has(cat.parent_id);
2669	+  const parentIds = new Set(
2670	+    categories.filter(cat => !hasValidParent(cat)).map(cat => cat.id),
2671	+  );
2672	+  const subcategoriesByParent = new Map<CategoryEntity['id'], T[]>();
2673	+  const topLevel: T[] = [];
2674	+
2675	+  for (const cat of categories) {
2676	+    if (cat.parent_id && parentIds.has(cat.parent_id)) {
2677	+      const siblings = subcategoriesByParent.get(cat.parent_id) ?? [];
2678	+      siblings.push(cat);
2679	+      subcategoriesByParent.set(cat.parent_id, siblings);
2680	+    } else {
2681	+      topLevel.push(cat);
2682	+    }
2683	+  }
2684	+
2685	+  return topLevel.map(cat => ({
2686	+    ...cat,
2687	+    subcategories: subcategoriesByParent.get(cat.id) ?? [],
2688	+  }));
2689	+}
2690	+
2691	+/** Whether a category is a subcategory of another category. */
2692	+export function isSubcategory(category: Pick<CategoryEntity, 'parent_id'>) {
2693	+  return category.parent_id != null;
2694	+}

# Review PR #73: "[AI] Add subcategories on main budget page" (icsasso)

## Context

The user wants to review a teammate's PR: run tests on it and review the code. The PR is
already checked out locally (`feat/issue-54-mainbudgetpage-subcategories` @ `6c61ea4fa`,

`feat/issue-62-goal-card-scaffold`.

The PR adds one level of category nesting (`categories.parent_id` migration). Money for a
subcategory comes out of its parent's budget, capped at what the parent has.
Templates, cleanup and every "To Budget → subcategory" path are blocked. The UI adds an
indented row, an "Add subcategory" / "Make subcategory of…" / "Remove from parent" menu,
and a Σ total hint. The PR has about 2.7k lines of code and tests, plus a 19.8k-line AI log.

**GitHub CI tells us nothing.** Every check "failed" after exactly 24h, which means the
depot runners never ran on this fork. Local runs are the real signal.

No code edits and no GitHub comments. The output is a review report for the user.

## Step 1: Run tests (from repo root, read-only apart from caches)

1. `yarn install` (no dependency changes in the PR, so this should be a no-op).
2. `yarn typecheck`
3. `yarn lint` (watch `actual/no-untranslated-strings` on the literal `Σ` in
   `ParentTotalHint.tsx`).
4. Targeted unit tests:
   - `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test src/server/budget/subcategories.test.ts src/server/db/index.test.ts src/shared/categories.test.ts src/server/budget src/server/aql src/server/migrate`
   - `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test src/components/budget/util.test.ts src/budget/mutations.test.tsx src/components/budget`
5. Full suite: `yarn test` (lage), to catch regressions outside the touched folders.
6. E2E: `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run playwright test budget.test.ts --browser=chromium`
   (the three new "Budget subcategories" tests plus the existing budget tests).
7. Optional manual smoke test (`yarn start` → "Don't use a server" → "View demo"), following
   the PR's own steps. Also try the mobile budget page and the tracking budget type, which
   the PR's tests don't cover.

Report pass/fail with the actual output of each step.

## Step 2: Code review (diff already read in full; confirm these while testing)

Check each item against the running code before it goes in the report:

1. **API behavior change.** `api/budget-set-amount` (`packages/loot-core/src/server/api.ts:445`)
   now goes through `setCategoryBudget`. External scripts that budget a subcategory get
   silently capped and charged to the parent. Neither tests nor docs mention this.
2. **Mobile and other entry points.** Desktop hides "To Budget" in the cover menu and the
   ToBudget transfer menu, but the server now _throws_ for To Budget → subcategory. Check
   whether the mobile cover/transfer modals (`components/modals/*Cover*`, `*Transfer*`) still
   offer that option, which would surface a raw error to the user.
3. **Bulk actions skip the parent rule.** `set12MonthAvg` / `set6MonthAvg` /
   `copyPreviousMonth` write subcategories with plain `setBudget`, so a subcategory is funded
   from To Budget and can exceed its parent. Ask whether that's intended.
4. **"Make subcategory of…" on an existing category.** Its current money (from To Budget)
   stays, and any goal template it had silently stops applying (`goal-template.ts`
   `getTemplates` skip). The user gets no warning.
5. **Subcategory → "To Budget" transfers** are still allowed through the balance transfer
   menu (outflow only). Probably fine, but confirm it's intended.
6. **Minor:**
   - `updateCategory` (`budget/app.ts`) now writes `parent_id = null` on every category
     update, creating an extra sync message per rename or hide.
   - `ExpenseCategoryMonth` / tracking `CategoryMonth` add two sheet subscriptions per
     category-month cell.
   - Changing a parent's `cat_group` through `updateCategory` (not `moveCategory`) doesn't
     carry its children. `nestCategories` degrades safely.
7. **Positives to note:** the server validates nesting rules; `nestCategories` handles
   orphans and cycles from sync conflicts; the ambiguous `parent_id` fix is in
   `executors.ts`; deleting a parent un-nests its children; tests are thorough.
8. **Housekeeping:** the AI log contains terminal escape sequences (`gh pr diff` refuses
   to print it), and it makes up about 90% of the PR's line count. The release note is fine.

`v_transactions` (no new ambiguity); the migration timestamp is newest.
